children: Kalpana Pathak Mumbai: Reliance Industries (RIL) redirected fuel exports to East and South Africa, the Mediterranean and other European markets to capitalise on market opportunities caused by supply disruptions due to the West Asia conflict. This helped the private refiner boost its market share in these markets by about 50%, showed the company's September quarter financial presentation.

RIL also tapped opportunities in Australia, Kenya and Tanzania for premium gasoline grades, while enhancing diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) supplies to the Mediterranean. "In the case of diesel and jet fuel, we found opportunities in the Mediterranean market because of the loss of supply," said Srinivasan Tuttagunta, chief operating officer, supply and trading at RIL, per the presentation.

RIL's oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business emerged as the biggest driver of its fiscal second quarter earnings, reporting a 68% surge in Ebitda to a record 25,203 crore. O2C revenue grew 44% to 231,601 crore, led by high energy prices. The West Asia conflict has disrupted energy supply chains, resulting in a 41% year-on-year rise in crude oil prices and a 50-78% jump in transportation fuel prices.

RIL said it also supplied low-sulphur ATF to South Africa for the first time, opening up potential new export opportunities. The company's export strategy comes amid a sharp rise in global refining margins as geopolitical disruptions, refinery outages and declining fuel inventories tighten product supplies.

title: Expanded Fuel Exports to New Territory amid W Asia Crisis: RIL
